brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Two full-depth bins placed: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full in adjacent cells piece:0,0,0;full and piece:1,0,0;full. Props fork x2 staged to show utensil use and both bins visible in look view.

Configurator verifies geometry and mesh clearance only, not material waterproofing. Build uses solid bins (hex-bin-full, no drain holes) which contain items by shape, but 3D-printed parts are not verified as waterproof; material choice is user-determined and not checked here.

Configurator does not verify heat resistance, food safety or dishwasher durability. Parts are 3D-printed (material user chooses) and cannot be confirmed dishwasher safe by this system; no material/process can be claimed from the build view.

finish.summary: Built a compact 2-cell utensil holder with two adjacent full-depth solid bins (no drained variants) and staged with utensil props to show use. House rules applied (caps and joint bolts, meshClash clear). Waterproof and dishwasher-safe could not be verified: the configurator checks fit only and does not assess materials, heat or food safety, so those requirements are reported unmet.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
